webcam-test.q1: How do I test my webcam?
webcam-test.a1: Press Start camera and allow access. You should see yourself in the preview; the panel shows the camera's name, the real resolution and the frame rate. Take a photo to check sharpness and colour.
webcam-test.q2: The preview is black or the camera is not found. What now?
webcam-test.a2: Close other apps that use the camera (video calls, OBS), check the privacy shutter or the camera key on your laptop, pick another camera in the list, and allow camera access for the browser in your system settings.
webcam-test.q3: Why is the resolution lower than I chose?
webcam-test.a3: Your camera does not offer that size, so the browser picks its nearest mode. The panel always shows the size you actually get.
webcam-test.q4: Why is the frame rate low?
webcam-test.a4: Most webcams drop to 15 fps or less in dim light to expose longer. Add light, or pick a lower resolution; USB 2.0 hubs can limit 1080p too.
webcam-test.a5: No. The video stays in this tab, and photos are made on your device. Nothing is sent or stored.

gamepad-test.q1: How do I test my controller?
gamepad-test.a1: Connect it by USB or Bluetooth and press any button: browsers only show a controller after a button press. Then press every button and move both sticks; each button lights up while pressed and stays marked once it has worked.
gamepad-test.q2: How do I check stick drift?
gamepad-test.a2: Let go of both sticks. A healthy stick reads close to 0.00; above 0.05 is slight drift that most games hide with a dead zone, and 0.15 or more usually shows in games.
gamepad-test.a3: Xbox, PlayStation, Switch Pro and most USB or Bluetooth gamepads. With a “standard” layout the buttons get their names; other pads show numbered buttons and axes.
gamepad-test.q4: Why does Test vibration not work?
gamepad-test.a4: Vibration needs a browser that supports it (Chrome and Edge do) and a controller with motors. Some Bluetooth connections do not pass it through.
gamepad-test.a5: No. The controller is read in this tab with the Gamepad API; nothing is sent or stored.

dead-pixel.q1: How do I check for dead pixels?
dead-pixel.a1: Clean the screen, press Start full screen test and look closely at each colour. A dead pixel stays black on white, a stuck pixel stays one colour (often red, green or blue), and a hot pixel stays white on black.
dead-pixel.a2: Dust and smudges move or blur when you wipe the screen or change your viewing angle; a bad pixel stays sharp in the same spot on every colour it should change on.
dead-pixel.q3: Can a stuck pixel be fixed?
dead-pixel.a3: Sometimes: a stuck pixel can come back after hours of normal use. Dead pixels usually stay. This page does not flash colours quickly, which can trigger seizures.
dead-pixel.q4: How do I move between colours?
dead-pixel.a4: Click or tap, or press Space or →, for the next colour; ← goes back. Tap the left third of a touch screen to go back. Esc or × closes the test.
dead-pixel.a5: Yes. Where full screen is not available (iPhone), the colour covers the whole browser window; hide the toolbars by scrolling or turning the phone.

refresh-rate.q1: How does the refresh rate test work?
refresh-rate.a1: The page counts how often the browser draws a frame. Browsers draw once per screen refresh, so the time between frames gives the refresh rate in Hz.
refresh-rate.q2: Why does it show 60 Hz on my 144 Hz monitor?
refresh-rate.a2: Check the rate set in your system's display settings, the cable (older HDMI caps at 60 Hz at high resolutions) and battery saver. With two screens, the browser follows the one its window is on.
refresh-rate.a3: Frames that took about twice as long as normal: the screen showed the previous frame again. A few are normal while the page loads; many mean the computer or browser is busy.
refresh-rate.q4: What is the moving block for?
refresh-rate.a4: At a higher refresh rate the block moves in smaller steps and looks smoother and sharper. Compare speeds to see judder or blur.
refresh-rate.q5: Why did the number change when I switched tabs?
refresh-rate.a5: Hidden tabs get few or no frames, so the test starts over when you come back. Keep the tab in front for a few seconds for a steady reading.

touch-test.q1: How do I test my touch screen?
touch-test.a1: Put fingers on the pad and draw. Each finger gets its own colour and number. Then swipe over the whole pad: cells you have touched fill in, and any that will not fill show a dead zone.
touch-test.q2: How many fingers does my screen support?
touch-test.a2: Put down as many fingers as you can at once and read Most at once. Phones and tablets usually track 5–10; some laptops track only 2.
touch-test.a3: Most touch screens and mice do not measure pressure. Pens such as Apple Pencil and Surface Pen usually do.
touch-test.q4: Can I test the edges of the screen?
touch-test.a4: Press Full screen so the pad fills the screen, then swipe along every edge and corner.
touch-test.a5: No. Touches are drawn in this tab and forgotten when you clear or close it.

webcam-test.lead: Check that your webcam works and see its real resolution and frame rate. Nothing is uploaded.
webcam-test.s1b: Press Start camera and allow access in the browser prompt. The preview shows you, mirrored like a mirror.
webcam-test.s2b: The panel shows the camera's name, the resolution it really sends, the aspect ratio and the measured frame rate. Pick another camera or resolution to compare.
webcam-test.s3b: Press Take photo to check sharpness and colour, then Save photo to keep it. It never leaves your device.

gamepad-test.lead: Test every button, trigger and stick of a controller and check for stick drift. Nothing is uploaded.
gamepad-test.s1b: Plug in the controller or pair it by Bluetooth, then press any button. Browsers only show a controller after a press.
gamepad-test.s2b: Each button fills while pressed (triggers fill part way) and stays outlined once it has worked, so you can spot a dead one.
gamepad-test.s3b: Move both sticks to the edges, then let go. A resting stick should read near 0.00; 0.15 or more is drift.

dead-pixel.lead: Fill the screen with solid colours to find dead, stuck or hot pixels. Nothing is uploaded.
dead-pixel.s1b: Wipe the screen first so dust is not mistaken for a pixel. Preview a colour with the swatches.
dead-pixel.s2b: Press Start full screen test. Click, Space or → moves to the next colour; ← goes back.
dead-pixel.s3b: Look closely at each colour: a dot that stays black, white or one colour is a bad pixel. Esc or × closes the test.

refresh-rate.lead: See the refresh rate your screen and browser really run at. Nothing is uploaded.
refresh-rate.s1b: The test starts by itself. Leave the tab in front for a few seconds while it counts frames.
refresh-rate.s2b: The big number is your refresh rate in Hz, with the nearest standard rate, the frame time and skipped frames.
refresh-rate.s3b: The block moves at the chosen speed. At higher Hz it looks smoother; a jerky block with spikes in the graph means skipped frames.

touch-test.lead: Check how many fingers your touch screen tracks and find dead zones. Nothing is uploaded.
touch-test.s1b: Put one or more fingers on the pad and draw. Each finger gets its own colour and number.
touch-test.s2b: Touching now shows the fingers on the screen; Most at once keeps the highest count.
touch-test.s3b: Swipe over the whole pad, or press Full screen to reach the edges. Cells that never fill in mark a dead zone.
